title: [P2.10a prerequisite] Persist and read back a durable ProductContractRevision: event, writer, and full-revision store reader

  2. No revision EVENT type, no schema, no durable bytes written anywhere.
  3. No full-revision STORE READER. task-db1a8566's approval writer can only admit a shape-only ref, so its DoD-3 (resolve the stored approval triple to a durable ProductContractRevision) cannot be satisfied honestly.

WHY IT CANNOT BE SKIPPED OR MOCKED: a positive resolver arm built today would validate caller-supplied bytes or a hand-built fixture, FABRICATING revision existence and digest authority. Epic Rail 4 forbids leaving a P1 boundary mock-only, so narrowing task-db1a8566's DoD is not an available shortcut — that was already ruled out.

RAIL 8(B) IS THE ACCEPTANCE BAR: this row must register its CONSUMER EDGE, not merely land a module. A codec that exists and is called by nothing satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist. task-965cb2d6 burned 26 claim-and-release cycles on exactly that shape. When you plan the gates, assert WHO IMPORTS AND CALLS the writer and reader from production — not that the symbols are present.

NOTE FOR SCOPE: task-8e62300c separately names three files that are absent at HEAD — product-contract-gate-1-identity.ts, -reader.ts, -resolver.ts, and no resolver export from apps/daemon/src/index.ts. definitionOfDone: DoD-1 VERIFY-OR-BLOCK at claim, recorded in a row comment. Re-run at your own HEAD: (a) `git grep -n 'createProductContractRevision\|decodeProductContractRevisionBytes' HEAD -- apps packages ':(exclude)*.test.ts' ':(exclude)*/index.ts'` and confirm it still returns ONLY the two definitions in product-contract-codec.ts; (b) confirm no revision event type or durable writer exists. If either premise has changed, report blocked naming the probe rather than planning against a stale measurement.

DoD-2 A PRODUCTION WRITER persists a ProductContractRevision durably: a named event type, its schema, and encoded bytes committed through the real store. The revision digest is SERVER-DERIVED via deriveProductContractRevisionDigest from the admitted draft — a caller may not supply or influence the digest. A caller-supplied digest is refused with a stable reason code at a named layer.

DoD-3 A PRODUCTION FULL-REVISION READER resolves a stored revision back from durable bytes through decodeProductContractRevisionBytes, returning the complete revision (not a shape-only ref). Malformed or absent bytes refuse deterministically with a stable reason code and refusing layer, asserted by name in tests.

DoD-4 CONSUMER EDGE PROVEN, per Rail 8(B): after this row, `git grep -ln 'product-contract-codec' HEAD -- apps packages | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns MORE than the module's own .js bridge, and the writer and reader are each imported AND called from a production module — the import edge traced, not a grep count. Existence of the symbols is explicitly NOT sufficient evidence.

DoD-5 Round-trip and tamper proof over a FILE-BACKED store: a revision written by the writer is read back byte-identical by the reader; a mutated byte refuses with the exact code; replay of the same revision adds zero duplicate decision and event rows. Mutation drills each redden a NAMED arm with proven restore.

DoD-6 Gates standalone, foreground, unpiped, each with exit code and nonzero count line quoted: `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck` and `test`, plus `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and the focused suite. Repo-wide red is attributed by merge-base versus delivered owned-path delta and any foreign failure disclosed verbatim.
taskRails: Do not narrow task-db1a8566's DoD-3 as an alternative to building this. That shortcut was ruled out by architect-94dd67c9 on 2026-08-28 and again by governor-0af24e35 on 2026-08-29; Rail 4 forbids a mock-only P1 boundary.

The revision digest is SERVER-DERIVED. Never accept a caller-supplied digest, and never build a positive arm from a hand-made fixture standing in for a stored revision — that fabricates the exact authority this row exists to make real.

Rail 8(A): if the writer or reader changes an exported signature, type or roster, list EVERY caller the change reaches in affectedFiles at planning time, measured with `git grep -l`, including test siblings. The roster is not capped by Rail 6's line limits.

Coordinate with task-8e62300c before planning the reader: it names product-contract-gate-1-identity.ts, -reader.ts and -resolver.ts as absent. State explicitly in the plan whether this row delivers that reader or whether it stays 8e62300c's, so the two neither collide nor both skip it.

comments.content:
GOVERNOR NOTE ON THE DAEMON'S SPLIT WARNING — read before you split this row.

create_task warned: "Title contains 'and' — often two tasks wearing one title. Split unless the halves genuinely cannot land independently." That is a good default and I considered it. MY JUDGEMENT IS THAT THE HALVES CANNOT LAND INDEPENDENTLY, and here is the reasoning so you can overrule it knowingly rather than by accident:

  A WRITER ALONE CANNOT SATISFY DoD-4. Rail 8(B) requires a registered CONSUMER EDGE. A writer that persists revisions nothing ever reads is precisely the orphan shape this row exists to end — it would satisfy every existence grep while the feature stays unreachable. That is the failure that cost task-965cb2d6 twenty-six claim-and-release cycles.
  A READER ALONE CANNOT SATISFY DoD-3 OR DoD-5 HONESTLY. With no production writer, the only bytes available to read are hand-built fixtures — which fabricates the revision existence and digest authority that task rail 2 forbids and that Rail 4 refuses to accept as a P1 boundary proof.
  DoD-5's round-trip and tamper arms are inherently two-sided: written by the writer, read back byte-identical by the reader, one mutated byte refused. Neither half can carry that arm alone.

So the split the warning suggests would produce two rows that each cannot prove their own DoD, which is worse than one row that can. IF YOU DISAGREE, split it — but then you must also re-cut the DoDs so each half has an honest, provable acceptance bar, and say in both plans how the first half proves itself without the second. Do not split on the title alone and leave these DoDs attached to the halves.

SEPARATE AND REAL SPLIT QUESTION, which the warning did NOT catch and which matters more: task-8e62300c names product-contract-gate-1-identity.ts, -reader.ts and -resolver.ts as absent at HEAD, plus a missing resolver export from apps/daemon/src/index.ts. The READER in this row may or may not BE that gate-1-reader. Settle that explicitly in your plan. If it is the same reader, say so and let 8e62300c consume it; if not, name the boundary. Two rows silently both building or both skipping that reader is the collision worth preventing here — not the "and" in my title.

— governor-0af24e35, filed at the human's explicit instruction 2026-08-29 11:55Z

This row's DoD-1(a) probe is `git grep -n '...' HEAD -- apps packages`. `git grep <rev>` reads the COMMIT, so it is BLIND TO UNTRACKED FILES BY CONSTRUCTION. The lesson generalises: an ABSENCE premise must be probed untracked-inclusive (`git status --porcelain`, or `grep -r` over the worktree), never with `git grep <rev>` alone. A PRESENCE premise is fine at HEAD.

=== WHAT I AM NOT DOING, AND WHY ===
I am not planning this row. Doing so would put a second worker onto six files worker-8d70fe57 is editing right now, in a shared worktree where pathspec commits are FILE-granular while the collision is HUNK-granular — there is no pathspec that takes one worker's hunks and leaves the other's. Epic rail 2 is explicit: a finding already owned elsewhere is adopted or verified, never duplicated.
